To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
long chain fatty acids enhance calcium sequestrations in skeletal muscle SR.
palmitic acid, a long chain fatty acid, enhances calcium sequestraton by the sarcoplasmic rreticulum.

palmitic acid, a fatty acid that accumulates in the cytosolic space of the ischemic heart muscle, increases calcium sequestration in the sarcoplasmic (intracellular) reticulum of cardiac and skeletal muscle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of long chain fatty acids on sarcoplasmic function in ischemic myocardium.
the effects of palmitic and other fatty acids on calcium transport in the heart.
the effects of palmitic (PA) and oleic (OA) acids on calcium sequestrations by sarcoplasmatic reticulum vesicle (SR) from rabbit skeletal muscle and canine cardiac tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
palmitic acid enhances the ability of isolated sarcoplasmc reticulum to sequester calcium in vitro.
the effect of PA on calcium sequestraion by the sarcoplasmic Reticulum is concentration dependent and may be a function of its ability to increase the fluidity of the membrane.
palmitic acid, in a concentration range below its critical micellar concentration, enhances calcium binding by skeletal and canine cardiac sarcoplasmic-reticulum vesicles in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
palmitic acid, a fatty acid found to accumulate in ischemic myocardium, increases calcium sequestration in isolated skeletal and cardiac SR.

palmitic acid enhances Ca sequestration by cardiac and skeletal SR, and that this may be one mechanism by which palmitic acid may contribute to the early contractile depression observed during myocardial ischemia.
the accumulation of PA in the cytosolic space of the ischemic heart may be an important determinant of early depression of contractility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PA, a fatty acid that accumulates in the ischemic myocardial cell, enhances calcium sequestraton by SR.
fatty acid accumulation in the cytosolic compartment may contribute to early calcium sequestration and thus to the contractile dysfunction observed in ischemia.
PA can increase the ability of the SR to retain calcium, and that this ability to enhance calcium retention is present in both cardiac and skeletal muscle.
